bio: Élise I is the Souvren of Brightport and, alongside President Amélien van der Cruz of Occasue, joint head of state of the United Republics of Brightport and Occasue. She is the first Souvren of the House of Brightwell, a Franco-British family, and the first woman to reign in Brightport’s history.

Before taking the throne she worked in diplomacy. Her diplomatic achievements, personal humility and youth won her wide public support, and her accession on Secundus 11, 114 NSC, at the age of 28, marked a generational change after the fall of the House of Kennedy. The anniversary is celebrated every year as Crown Day.

Warm and approachable, she champions education, multilingualism, environmental conservation and reconciliation between nations, and favours a modern monarchy that balances royal pageantry with openness. She lives at Souvren Palace with her husband, Souvren Consort Julien, and their sons Théo and Lucas, who attend an ordinary public school. She began the Royal Open House, National School Visits and the Crown Day Garden Party. Her working relationship with President van der Cruz has grown from early tension into friendship.

bio: Amélien van der Cruz is the 24-year-old President of the Republic of Occasue and, alongside Souvren Élise I of Brightport, joint head of state of the United Republics of Brightport and Occasue. A member of the Republican Left, he rose to national prominence through student activism, becoming a leading voice for a youth movement concerned with housing affordability and the cost of living. He won his party’s presidential nomination against established political figures.

Raised in a working-class family by a railway worker and a nurse, van der Cruz studied political science and international relations. His family descends from Nyreth’s original settlers, with generations of mixed Afro-Latino American, Dutch and French ancestry. He speaks all six of URBO’s official languages.

Known for his charismatic, approachable and optimistic manner, he lives relatively modestly and still visits the neighbourhood he grew up in. Outside politics, he enjoys football, gaming and music. His working relationship with Souvren Élise I has grown from early tension into friendship.

overview: Brightport and Occasue keep their own armed forces, joined under a permanent Joint Military Command. They are not merged into one federal force.
Three branches: land, sea (maritime) and aerospace. Cyber defence runs through all three; there is no separate cyber or space force.
Doctrine: defensive neutrality. URBO defends its sovereignty and stays out of foreign wars.
Supreme military command belongs jointly to the Souvren of Brightport and the President of Occasue, acting as the joint heads of state of URBO. Neither can exercise it alone.
About 1.5 to 2 million people serve on active duty. A voluntary professional reserve of former personnel and trained volunteers backs them up.
Defence spending is 2 to 3% of the economy.
AI only advises: it helps with analysis and paperwork, but people make every decision.
Research and development is a partnership of government laboratories, private firms and universities.
branches: Professional soldiers with advanced equipment and advisory AI. In peacetime: training, disaster relief, humanitarian help, building infrastructure and helping remote communities.

Separate republican fleets plus permanent joint formations. In peacetime: guarding the coast and territorial waters, search and rescue, protecting the environment and shipping, and helping navigation.

Republican aviation divisions plus the shared Joint Space Division. Protects the airspace and orbit, rescues aircraft and spacecraft, monitors disasters and supports science and the URBO Space Agency.
space: The Joint Space Division belongs to the aerospace branch and is shared by both republics.
It works in permanent partnership with the civilian URBO Space Agency: shared research, emergency help and some infrastructure, with separate jobs.

URBO takes part in a shared international presence on the moons, with cooperative installations alongside other Nyrethian nations, for research, communications, rescue and peacekeeping. No country claims the moons.
service: Every citizen, of every gender, does one Nyreth year of national service (300 days), starting at a time of their choice between 18 and 25 Earth years old.
Service can be military or civilian: education, healthcare, elderly care, conservation, farming, restoring the environment, public works, transport, or disaster relief and emergency services.
People recruit into their own republic’s forces, with chances to serve in the other republic.
While serving, people get a service allowance of Ⓑ1,800 a month on top of the Ⓑ1,200 basic income: Ⓑ3,000 a month, or Ⓑ30,000 over the year, before any tax.
Refusing without an approved exemption brings warnings, help, alternative assignments and finally penalties.
history: After the Treaty of Berevo, each republic kept its own forces, and both pulled troops back from the border. Brightport kept most of the old military bases; Occasue rebuilt its forces.
The Joint Military Command came after reunification, through gradual integration.
The forces have a mixed identity: separate republican uniforms, flags and traditions, but the same working uniforms. Friendly rivalry and banter go along with real cooperation.
deserto: Ft. Deserto is a major garrison city: a headquarters and administrative centre, a research and training complex, and home to permanent military communities.
Deserto has more military installations than anywhere else. They are run by the Brightport Armed Forces within the joint framework.
Ordinary towns sit alongside restricted sites. Every state has some permanent military presence, each with its own speciality.
Details of installations in Deserto are not available to the public.

life: The feel of everyday technology
life
Advanced but grounded: daily life is recognisable, with clever materials, automation and smart infrastructure rather than a sci-fi look.
AI runs much of the transport, infrastructure and routine work.
Energy comes from commercial fusion, renewables and conventional nuclear power together.
Smartphones, wearables and holographic devices exist side by side, and physical objects still matter to people.
Getting around
transport
Electric and hydrogen cars are both common. Most cars drive themselves by default, but driving by hand is still legal.
Railways mix ordinary trains, high-speed lines and maglev on different routes.
In big cities, public transport rules: metros, trams, buses and walking. Berevo’s Stadsspoor is one example.
Planes run mainly on synthetic, carbon-neutral fuel. Regional flights are subsonic, international ones supersonic, and premium hypersonic flights exist.
Personal devices and AI helpers
devices
People use AI assistants on their devices, personal AI companions that follow them across devices, and holographic AI avatars.
Smart glasses are optional; AR glasses and contact lenses are common; public spaces have interactive displays.
Homes have specialised robots, general-purpose humanoid robots and built-in smart systems.
Real-time translation by app, earbuds, glasses or holographic interpreter is everywhere, yet URBO’s six official languages and language lessons still matter.
Health
health
People in URBO live to about 110 to 120 Earth years on average.
Prevention, early detection and cures all play a part, though no single disease has been wiped out.
Lab-grown organs, tissue regrowth and both biological and mechanical replacements are available.
Healthcare is public and paid for by the government.
AI helps doctors, but a human doctor always makes the final call.
Genetic engineering of people is allowed only for serious medical conditions. Fertility treatment usually works; artificial wombs are not used.
Cybernetic enhancements exist but are unusual: most people prefer their bodies unmodified.
Homes and cities
homes
Each region builds in its own style, so Brightport City and Berevo look clearly different.
Homes range from smart and automated to self-maintaining.
Buildings go up by hand craft, robots, 3D printing and factory-built modules.
Cities recycle, recover water, plant rooftop gardens, parks and green corridors, and use AI to save energy and water.
School, work and retirement
work
Classrooms are still led by human teachers, who use modern tools but familiar methods. AI does not replace teachers.
Much routine work is automated, so most people work in creative, social, scientific or supervisory jobs.
High wages, a universal basic income and public services work together.
The usual retirement age is 65 Earth years.
The working week follows the calendar: four six-hour work days in each ten-day week.
Food, farms and wildlife
nature
Farming mixes automated fields, vertical farms and automated greenhouses. Lab-grown meat and farmed animals both exist.
Some native ecosystems look Earth-like, others truly alien, and Earth and native species have mixed a great deal since the landing.
Pets are mostly Earth animals: dogs, cats, fish and the like.
Some native creatures look familiar, others are completely unfamiliar. Some native foods are safe to eat, some need processing, and some are unsafe.
URBO has large national parks, restores damaged land, and watches the environment with AI, satellites and drones.
Internet, identity and privacy
internet
Nyreth has its own planetary internet, with gateways to Earth’s networks (slow ones, because of the distance).
Internet and phone service are mainly public utilities.
People use government digital IDs, biometrics and their own privacy controls, but physical ID cards and passports are still common and valued.
Privacy laws are strict: collecting personal data needs clear permission.
Entertainment comes on ordinary screens, in VR and as holograms.

facts: Travel to Earth
Near-light-speed ships make the trip in about one Earth year each way. Space travel keeps Earth time, because people from Earth set it up.
Spaceports
Ships leave straight from spaceports on the ground. URBO has two: at Brightport City and at Berevo.
On board
Passengers can travel awake or in induced hibernation.
Operators
Both public and private companies fly between the stars. The leading passenger carrier is TerraLink.
URBO Space Agency
URBO’s national space agency.
The moons
Commercial trips to Nyreth’s moons exist but are expensive. There are no permanent settlements on the moons.
Who travels

Space travel is rare for ordinary people in every country on Nyreth. Even the rich seldom go, because of the time it takes. Some people save for a lifetime to visit Earth’s historic sites when they retire.
Earth Research Fellowship
A government scholarship for top students to do research on Earth. Like the Rhodes Scholarship, but even more prestigious. URBO also pays for diplomatic missions to Earth.
Messages
Urgent messages travel by advanced systems. Ordinary data is slower, and films and shows take about three months to arrive, in either direction.

facts: Most banking is done by public, government-owned banks, though private banks are not banned.
Every adult citizen gets the same monthly universal basic income. It is a safety net, not a replacement for a wage: people can work to earn more, and are expected to take part when they can.
The universal basic income is Ⓑ1,200 a month, the same everywhere: Ⓑ12,000 a year.
Yearly figures, such as average incomes, are counted in Nyreth years of ten months.
Paid work and recognised study both count as taking part.

Refusing work without good reason carries social stigma and, step by step, government action: warnings, help finding work, and finally financial penalties. Not being able to find work is not the same as refusing it.
URBO is prosperous but not perfect: unemployment and homelessness still exist.
Income tax is progressive. Most tax is collected federally and shared out to the republics by need, with extra support for poorer regions.

facts: The Nyrethian Standard Calendar (NSC) counts from the first human landing: Primus 1, year 1.
A year has exactly 300 days: ten months of 30 days. There are no leap years, so every year looks the same.
A week has ten days, and every month is exactly three weeks. Every month starts on Caeloris and ends on Neptunis.
The year starts at the beginning of spring. There are five seasons of 60 days each: Spring, Summer, Harvest, Autumn and Winter.
People work two days, rest three, work two and rest three. The rest breaks are called Inner Recess and Outer Recess. A working day lasts six Earth hours.
Work days are named after Nyreth’s four moons. Recess days are named after planets of Earth’s solar system.
A day lasts 26 Earth hours. Clocks are decimal: 10 hours in a day, 100 minutes in an hour, 100 seconds in a minute. A clock reading 5.42 is just past the middle of the day.
Dates are written month/day/year, for example 08/15/0119 NSC.
Nyreth has ten time zones, one hour apart, measured from an international observatory. Standard time is called NST.
Public holidays fall on fixed dates. A holiday that lands on a Recess day gets a replacement rest day. Each state may add three holidays of its own.
URBO covers three time zones. The sun rises in the west, so the west is ahead: Occasue Time is two hours ahead of Brightport Time, with Mountain Time in between.

timeline.text: A three-year war over territory, trade and rival alliances. Schoonheid loses its west coast through a peace agreement and local referendums. The war deepens Brightport’s own divisions.

timeline.name: The first Souvren
timeline.text: Brightport creates the Souvren to give the nation unity, identity and stability. John I of the House of Kennedy is nominated by representatives and approved by public vote. The country keeps the name “Republic”.

timeline.name: Brightportish Civil War
timeline.text: Unequal rebuilding money, refused demands for western autonomy and an attempt by the west to leave bring war. The new monarchy is a lesser cause. The war is short and not especially bloody, and neutral nations mediate its end.

timeline.name: Treaty of Berevo: Occasue independent
timeline.text: The country is formally divided into Brightport and Occasue. Divided families get travel permits, the right to dual citizenship and help to reunite. Relations are cold but peaceful, with checkpoints along the new border.

timeline.name: Reconciliation begins
timeline.text: Trade, family and cultural ties draw the republics back together through cooperation, negotiations and referendums. Hardliners in Berevo oppose closer ties.

timeline.name: Joseph I becomes Souvren
timeline.text: John I dies of natural causes while reigning. His son Joseph I succeeds him.

timeline.name: URBO founded
timeline.text: The Charter of Union is signed in Lochwater. Some border checkpoints are demolished, some are kept as monuments and others become visitor centres and service areas. The day is now Constitution Day.

timeline.name: Joseph I removed
timeline.text: The Gardiens remove Joseph I from the throne. His brother Patrick I becomes the third Souvren.

timeline.name: The House of Brightwell takes the crown
timeline.text: After money scandals, political meddling and public protests, the House of Kennedy is disqualified and returns to ordinary citizenship. Élise I becomes Souvren, the first woman to reign. The day is now Crown Day.

timeline.name: The present day
timeline.text: URBO is a young union, about twelve Earth years old. The site’s calendar started at 08/15/0119 and runs live.

origin: The Souvren was created about year 89 NSC, after the First Nyreth World War, to give Brightport unity, cultural identity and political stability.
The first Souvren was nominated by representatives and approved by a public vote.
Brightport kept the name “Republic” even with a monarch.

houses.name: House of Kennedy
houses.note: The founding dynasty: an American old-money family descended from the Kennedy political family of Earth. A branch of the family took part in the first settlement of Nyreth. It lost public trust through elitism, political meddling and money scandals, and was disqualified by the Gardiens (under the rules of the time).
rulers: The first Souvren. Died of natural causes while reigning. Father of Joseph I and Patrick I.
Son of John I. Removed from the throne by the Gardiens.
Son of John I and brother of Joseph I. His reign ended when the dynasty was disqualified.

houses.name: House of Brightwell
houses.note: The second dynasty: a Franco-British family.
rulers: The first woman to reign. A former diplomat, 28 at her accession and about 33 today.

elise: Before becoming Souvren, Élise I worked in diplomacy. Her diplomatic record, her humility and her youth won public support after the Kennedy years.
She is warm and approachable. Her causes are education, multilingualism, conservation and reconciliation between nations.
She favours a modern monarchy: royal pageantry, but open and easy to reach.
family: Souvren Consort, her husband. A physician before joining the royal household.
Elder son, aged 8. First in line to the throne.
crown.family_note: Both boys go to an ordinary public school with other Brightportish children.
crown.palace: The royal residence is Souvren Palace, built in the style of a French château.
traditions: Citizens may visit parts of Souvren Palace.
The Souvren visits schools across Brightport.
Members of the public celebrate Crown Day (Secundus 11) with the royal family.

who: The Council of Gardiens has nine members.
They are elected by the Brightport Parliament.
Each serves an eight-year term. Terms are staggered, and members may be re-elected without limit.
Gardiens must stay out of party politics while serving, and may not belong to a party.
They come from mixed backgrounds: lawyers alongside people from other professions and public service.
powers: At least 6 votes of 9 (two thirds). Removing one Souvren does not by itself disqualify the family.
All 9 Gardiens must agree. The family returns to ordinary citizenship and loses its titles.
The Brightport Parliament nominates candidates, and the citizens of Brightport elect the new Souvren, who founds a new hereditary line.

If the Souvren is incapacitated, the heir is under age, or the country is waiting to elect a new dynasty, the Gardiens appoint a temporary Regent. The Regent also carries out Brightport’s share of the federal head-of-state duties. The Souvren Consort has no automatic right to the role.
Reviewed by the High Court first, then by Parliament.
gardiens.succession: The crown passes to the eldest child, whatever their gender, under the Gardiens’ oversight.

landmarks: The tall tower with the pointed crown, the tallest in the city. Finished soon after the peace treaty as a symbol of the new union.
areas: Well-off neighbourhood on the bluffs above the Brightport River.
Narrow streets and the homes of the first settlers.
Busy and full of markets and food halls.
Commuter suburb on the Capital Line.
food: The city’s signature dish: a round, golden savoury pie with a pastry sun on top.
sports: Football club, nicknamed the Suns. Football is the city’s main sport.
Brightport City FC against Berevo United, the biggest match in URBO: the two capitals, east against west. First played the year the peace treaty was signed.
UBA basketball, Brightport Conference. Plays at Souvren Arena (32,000 seats); 11 titles. Souvren Élise I is honorary patron.
Football club, nicknamed the Harbourmen. Colours: orange and black. The crest shows a lion and an anchor, for the city’s Dutch and seafaring roots.
Orange smoke before kick-off, a sea of orange scarves and singing, and harbour horns whenever Berevo United scores.
Berevo United against Brightport City FC, the biggest match in URBO. First played the year the peace treaty was signed.
UBA basketball, Occasue Conference and reigning champions. Plays at De Zonarena, the Berevo Sun Arena (25,000 seats); 11 titles.
berevo.pop: 10 million in the city and 20 million in Greater Berevo.
landmarks: A pearl-white cable-stayed bridge, 8.2 km long. It carries road traffic, Stadsspoor trains, cycleways and footpaths. It was built to celebrate Occasue’s independence and republican identity.
The 90,000-seat home of Berevo United, in Downtown.
The main venue of the Berevo International Film Festival.
transport: The metro: 26 lines, branded in orange and white. “Stadsspoor” is Dutch for city railway.
On the eastern edge of the city, linked directly by Stadsspoor.
events: Held every year in Tertius, the first month of summer. It mixes big premieres, independent films, new filmmakers and blockbusters. Its top prize is the Golden Lion.

continents: Uropon is the larger eastern continent, home to Rhine, Instania and Guinesem.
Asuna is the smaller continent south of Uropon, with Juku, Tinsha and New China.
Anracia is the western continent, home to URBO, Schoonheid, Joya and Shinchied.
notes: The dashed blue lines are early shipping routes from Brightport, as drawn on the 2180 map.
The First Nyreth World War (NWWI) was a global skirmish. Schoonheid lost its west coast in it, and it led on to the Brightportish civil war.
The area inside Guinesem is disputed territory.
changes: URBO now holds the whole west coast of its continent. On the 2180 drawing, Schoonheid wrapped around the north-west.
Swisswa, once a Schoonheid town on that coast, is now a town in Ouest. Many Schoon loyalists remain there.
The Brightport colony of Twinshied became Norham, and now lies closer to the mainland, off the south-east coast.
On the drawing, Brightport was one republic. It is shown here as the two republics of URBO.

planet: On Nyreth the sun rises in the west and sets in the east, because the planet spins the opposite way to Earth.
Because of that spin, the prevailing winds over URBO blow from east to west, so storms usually arrive from the east.
Nyreth has four moons: Caelora, Nix, Aureth and Silvara. They appear in the original pencil drawing of the Brightport City skyline, and four weekdays are named after them.
A day on Nyreth lasts 26 Earth hours, and a year lasts 300 days.
Nyreth keeps in touch with Earth, but travel between the two planets is rare.

solis.origin: The sun on every Brightport flag began as the emblem of Solis, and the state is named for it: Solis means “of the sun.” The first colony ships landed here, and Brightport City grew from their landing camp.
solis.known: Solis is the nation’s finance and business hub, home to the ministries, the banks and the national stock exchange in Brightport City. The Souvren lives here, which gives the state its nickname.
trad: The Festival of Lanterns: on the longest night, lanterns float down the Brightport River.
solis.symbol: The rising sun, shown on the shield of the Solis flag.

floribus.origin: Settlers found the coast covered in wildflowers every spring, so they named it Floribus, “with flowers.”
floribus.known: Floribus is the nation’s warm-weather getaway, known for its beaches and holidays. The Port of Trempas, flower and fruit farms and seafood from Trempas Bay keep its economy busy all year.
trad: The Blessing of the Fleet: each season the fishing boats of Trempas Bay are decorated and blessed.
floribus.climate: Warm and breezy, with sea breezes keeping it mild all year.

estercrystal.origin: Settlers found caves of glittering quartz in the eastern hills and named the land for them; “ester” means east.
estercrystal.known: Estercrystal is known for gems and glassmaking: crystal mines in the hills and famous glassworks in its shires.
trad: Crystal Night: on the first night of winter, crystal lamps and candles set in crystals light every window.

weiden.origin: The name comes from a lost word of the first settlers, meaning “high country.”
weiden.known: Weiden is known for skiing and winter sports on the slopes around Bikbergen.
trad: Midsummer Night: bonfires, maypoles, flower crowns and dancing on the longest day.
weiden.symbol: A water-mill wheel: mills on its mountain streams powered the first settlements.

sur.origin: Settlers from Earth’s Spanish-speaking south named it in their own language: Sur, “south.” Nobody remembers where the name of Mami City comes from; it is lost to time.
sur.known: Sur is known for copper mining in its mesas, around the town of Cobre.
trad: Farolito Night: paper lanterns line every roof, street and path in winter.

norham.origin: The islanders voted to join Brightport for protection and trade. Norham added the sixth ray to the sun on Brightport’s flags.
norham.known: Norham is one of the wealthiest places in URBO, an island retreat for old money, much like Nantucket. Its harbour still lands the nation’s best seafood.
trad: The Harbour Festival: boat parades and seafood stalls along the Silverstone waterfront.
norham.more: Norham is known, not always kindly, for its snobbery. Islanders speak with a posh accent that mainlanders love to imitate.
norham.transport: Robust public transport: the Island Railway loop, island buses to every village, and a ferry to Brightport City. Lochway N1 links Silverstone and Harbourmouth.

deserto.origin: Ft. Deserto was founded as the base of the first expedition to cross the desert.
deserto.known: Deserto is known for huge solar farms and large, very secretive military installations. Stories of aliens are part of local culture, a running joke on a planet where the aliens are the humans from Earth.
trad: The Night Market: markets open only after sunset, when the desert cools.

kus.origin: The name comes from the Dutch word “kust,” coast, brought by early Dutch settlers.
kus.known: Kus is home to Berevo, the capital of Occasue and the political heart of the republic.
trad: Republic Day: celebrates Occasue choosing a president over a monarch.

ouest.origin: Ouest is named after the French settlers’ company, the Compagnie du Grand Ouest.
ouest.known: Ouest is known for French food and wine: bread, cheese, vineyards and village markets.
trad: The Fête du Vin, a week-long wine festival.
ouest.more: The coastal town of Swisswa once belonged to Schoonheid. It still resents being taken into URBO, and many Schoon loyalists live there.

levels.name: URBO federal government
levels.body: URBO National Parliament: Assembly (300) and Council of States (32)
facts: URBO is a balanced federation of two republics under a common federal constitution, a bicameral parliament, one court system and a shared citizenship.

The joint heads of state are the Souvren of Brightport and the President of Occasue. Each is also head of state of their own republic. They have equal federal authority: neither outranks the other, and any federal decision that needs head-of-state approval needs both.
If the two disagree, the URBO National Parliament mediates and proposes compromises, but cannot impose a decision. Legal and constitutional disputes go to the URBO High Court.
The Prime Minister of URBO runs the federal government. The joint heads of state appoint the prime minister, who must keep the confidence of Parliament.

The federal prime ministership passes to the other republic after every scheduled five-year federal election. The deputy prime minister always comes from the other republic, and cabinet posts (apart from the PM) are split equally between the republics.
Every federal bill must pass both chambers, which have equal power, and then receive assent from both heads of state. Parliament cannot override a refusal.
The federal constitution and federal law take precedence over republican constitutions and laws.
Most taxes are collected federally and shared out to the republics according to population, economic development, infrastructure and public-service needs, with extra support for poorer regions.

levels.name: Republic of Brightport
facts: Brightport keeps its hereditary monarchy despite its historical name as a republic. The Souvren is the sovereign of the people, not the ruler of the land.
The Souvren is head of state of Brightport and a joint head of state of URBO.

The Brightport Parliament has 120 seats elected by proportional representation. It elects the Prime Minister of Brightport, elects the nine Gardiens, and nominates candidates when a new royal dynasty is needed.
The prime minister runs Brightport’s day-to-day government, separately from the federal prime minister.
Brightport has its own constitution, which must comply with the federal constitution.
Six states and Deserto Territory. Brightportish language and culture are emphasised.
Current Souvren: Élise I of the House of Brightwell. Prime minister: Nathaniel Fairbourne.

levels.name: Republic of Occasue
facts: Occasue keeps its republican system and its ancestral Earth languages and cultures, with Brightportish secondary.
The President of Occasue is head of state of Occasue and a joint head of state of URBO.

The President and Vice President are elected together by Occasue citizens only, for five years with no term limit, in a two-round election: over 50% wins outright, otherwise the top two go to a runoff.
Candidates for president must be at least 18 Earth years old.
The Vice President is deputy head of state within Occasue, and becomes President, and joint head of URBO, if the President dies, resigns or is removed.

The Occasue Parliament has 120 seats elected by proportional representation. It elects the Prime Minister of Occasue, who runs day-to-day government, and can start impeachment proceedings against the President. The URBO High Court decides whether there are constitutional grounds for removal.
Occasue has its own constitution, which must comply with the federal constitution.
Four states and Montes Territory.
Current president: Amélien van der Cruz. Vice president: Mathieu van Dijk. Prime minister: Ewan Dunmore.

levels.name: State governments
facts: URBO has ten semi-autonomous states, each with an elected governor and an elected legislature.
States make laws on limited matters and run some local affairs, infrastructure and public services, within republican and federal law.
The six Brightport states are the six rays of Brightport’s sun; the four Occasue states are the four rays of Occasue’s sun.

levels.name: Territorial governments
facts: Deserto (Brightport) and Montes (Occasue) are run directly by their republic’s government, through an appointed administrator. They have no elected state government.
Territories sit alongside states, not beneath them, and do not count as rays on the flags.
Each territory directly elects one member of the Council of States and keeps its Assembly seats.

exec: The Souvren and the President jointly appoint the federal prime minister, who must keep Parliament’s confidence.
The prime ministership passes to the other republic after every scheduled five-year federal election. The rotation belongs to the republic, not the person.
By a parliamentary vote of no confidence, or by a joint decision of both heads of state. Neither can dismiss the prime minister alone.
If the prime minister dies, resigns or is removed, the heads of state appoint a replacement from the same republic for the rest of the term. This does not trigger the rotation.
The prime minister appoints the deputy and the ministers, half from each republic. The heads of state do not need to approve them.

assembly: 300 seats, shared out by population; every state and territory has at least one.

Elected by mixed-member proportional representation: each voter casts a constituency vote for a local member and a party vote. Party-list seats top up the constituency seats so the result is proportional.
council: 32 seats: three for each of the ten states and one for each territory (19 for Brightport, 13 for Occasue).
Of each state’s three members, two are elected by its citizens and one is appointed by the state legislature. Each territory elects its one member directly: 22 elected and 10 appointed in all.
both: The two chambers have equal power. Every federal bill must pass both, and neither can override the other.
Every bill then needs assent from both the Souvren and the President. Parliament cannot override a refusal, but may mediate and encourage a compromise.
Elections every five years. The scheduled election triggers the rotation of the federal prime ministership.

constitution: URBO has three constitutions: the Constitution of URBO, the Constitution of the Republic of Brightport and the Constitution of the Republic of Occasue.
The federal constitution is supreme. Republican constitutions must comply with it, and federal law prevails over republican law. State laws must comply with both.

Amending the URBO Constitution needs a supermajority in both chambers of the URBO parliament, approval from both the Brightport and the Occasue parliaments, and consent from both heads of state. Neither republic can have an amendment imposed on it.
judiciary: One integrated court system. Brightport and Occasue run their own courts.

The URBO High Court is the highest court of appeal for every case, the final word on the federal constitution, and the court for constitutional disputes between governments and between the heads of state.
It also decides whether there are constitutional grounds to remove the President of Occasue.
funding: Most tax is collected by the federal government and shared out to Brightport and Occasue, which run their own budgets and public services.
The share depends on population, economic development, infrastructure and public-service needs. Poorer regions get extra support to narrow the gaps.
calendar: Start of the five-year federal term
The URBO Assembly, the elected members of the Council of States, and the President and Vice President of Occasue. The federal prime ministership rotates.
The Brightport and Occasue parliaments, which then elect their prime ministers.
citizenship: Every citizen holds URBO citizenship plus citizenship of either Brightport or Occasue. Each republic issues its own passport: yellow for Brightport, red for Occasue.
Citizens may travel, live, work, study and use public services in either republic without any permit.
Federal voting rights are shared. Republican voting rights follow republican citizenship: a Brightport citizen living in Occasue cannot vote in Occasue’s republican or presidential elections.
A citizen may apply to change republican citizenship after living five years in the other republic.

Children born in URBO take the republican citizenship of the republic they are born in. Children born abroad to URBO citizens take their parent’s republican citizenship; if the parents differ, the parents choose.

Foreign nationals may apply after ten years’ legal residence, with good conduct, a language of their new republic, knowledge of its government and history, and an oath of allegiance to URBO. Dual nationality is allowed only with countries that have a reciprocal agreement with URBO.

election_rules: Every citizen is registered automatically at 18 Earth years.
Voting is compulsory. Not voting without a good reason brings a Ⓑ100 fine.
Paper ballots only, counted by optical scanners, with mandatory hand audits.
An independent Federal Electoral Commission runs every election.
A party needs 3% of the vote to win list seats in the Assembly.
The official campaign lasts 60 Nyreth days. Televised debates are compulsory for every qualifying candidate. Private donations are allowed with strict transparency.
Candidates for President of Occasue must be at least 18 Earth years old.

notes: Amélien van der Cruz and his running mate, Mathieu van Dijk of the Green Party, won in the first round, so no runoff was needed. The Green Party endorsed van der Cruz.

Laurent Delacroix, a former Prime Minister of Occasue, led the Western Liberal ticket. His government had failed to deliver affordable housing while prices kept rising, and Western Liberal support in Kus collapsed. Van der Cruz campaigned on housing and the cost of living and promised mass construction of affordable homes.
The two are fierce rivals in public.

eras.summary: The original yellow country between Schoonheid and Joya, governed from Brightport City: seven states, Deserto Territory and the capital territory.

eras.summary: Western states grow dissatisfied with centralization in Brightport City, economic neglect and disregard for western culture. The conflict builds gradually, not from one event.

eras.summary: A global skirmish among the countries of Nyreth. Schoonheid lost its west coast, which is now part of URBO, and the war led on to the Brightportish civil war.

eras.name: Civil war
eras.summary: A relatively short and not especially bloody war shows the unified republic is politically unsustainable.

eras.name: Peace treaty
eras.summary: The country is formally divided into Brightport and Occasue. Laws, currency, road signs, borders and institutions change; the treaty includes provisions for divided families.

eras.name: Early separation
eras.summary: For the first few years the new international border has extensive checkpoints and controls.

eras.name: Rapprochement
eras.summary: Within a few years relations improve greatly. Together the two republics are a major power on Nyreth. Hardliners in Berevo oppose closer ties.

eras.name: URBO
eras.summary: The republics form a shared federal system, as if the US and the EU had a baby. Checkpoints are removed and people move freely across the union. Each republic keeps its own government.
